key_insight: Imperfect physics improves regression rates only below a modeling-error threshold; with exact physics, studied PDE classes yield rates corresponding to dimension d−1 rather than d.
engineering_relevance: The results help assess when PDE constraints can improve sample efficiency and provide conditions for near-linear computation and tuning without knowing the modeling error.
method: Benchmark physics-informed regression against learning with smoothness alone.
Derive modeling-error thresholds for every linear PDE and certain nonlinear PDEs.
Establish error-dependent rates for constant-coefficient elliptic and hyperbolic PDE classes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees and minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors, but no empirical datasets or experiments.
watch_item: Detailed rate improvements are established for specific constant-coefficient PDE classes and should not be assumed for arbitrary physical models.
paper_title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
